coreVocabulary.definitionEn: to copy something exactly or produce something similar
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Online interactions cannot fully replicate the benefits of face-to-face friendships.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: to affect a situation in a negative way or stop something from working properly
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Excessive phone notifications constantly interfere with students' concentration.

coreVocabulary.meaningAr: مرضٍ / مشبع / ذو جدوى وإشباع نفسي
coreVocabulary.definitionEn: making you feel happy, satisfied, and complete
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Volunteering in the local community can be a deeply fulfilling leisure pursuit.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: paying conscious attention to the present moment and daily choices
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Teenagers should be mindful of the daily hours they dedicate to social apps.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: limits or rules that show what is acceptable, safe, or allowed
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Parents and teens must set clear digital boundaries around bedtime screen use.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: to take or move out or back, or to pull away from social interaction
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Heavy gamers may withdraw from family gatherings and direct peer conversations.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: causing a very strong need or desire to keep doing or using something repeatedly
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Endless algorithm feeds are deliberately engineered to be addictive.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: an uncomfortable feeling of nervousness or worry about something that is happening
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Fear of missing out on social media often fuels acute teenage anxiety.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: time when you are free from work, school, or obligations and can relax or enjoy hobbies
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Constructive leisure time recharges mental energy and sparks genuine creativity.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the amount of time a person spends using devices with screens like phones and laptops
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Limiting daily screen time helps protect sleep hygiene and eye health.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the way you feel about your own value, abilities, and importance
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Unfavorable online comparisons can severely undermine an adolescent's self-esteem.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a recognized clinical pattern where digital gaming displaces essential life routines
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: The WHO officially classified gaming disorder as a health condition needing attention.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the state of a person's emotional, psychological, and social well-being
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Physical exercise and creative hobbies are vital pillars of sound mental health.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: a widespread situation in which people do not get enough physical exercise
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Sedentary screen habits have created an alarming movement crisis among teenagers.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: involving people or teams striving to outdo others and win

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the genuine feeling of pleasure and satisfaction derived from an activity
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Physical leisure must prioritize personal enjoyment over sheer winning.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: to continue striving determinedly despite hardships, setbacks, or fatigue
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Athletes who persevere through difficult training routines reach their ultimate goals.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the ability to communicate, cooperate, and resolve differences constructively with peers
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Team sports significantly boost an adolescent's interpersonal social competence.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the physical and mental stamina to sustain prolonged exertion under pressure
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Marathon runners build supreme endurance through gradual, disciplined conditioning.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: practical abilities enabling individuals to cope effectively with daily life demands
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Time management, teamwork, and coping with defeat are essential life skills.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: relating to mental states, emotional processes, and behavioral patterns
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Regular exercise yields powerful psychological benefits, combating stress and fatigue.

coreVocabulary.definitionEn: the legitimate right, means, or opportunity to enter, use, or participate in something
coreVocabulary.exampleEn: Every neighbourhood should guarantee open access to safe public sports facilities.

skills.titleEn: Advanced Baccalaureate Writing Skills: Opinion Paragraph & Diary Entry
skills.titleAr: مهارات الكتابة المتقدمة: فقرة إبداء الرأي واليوميات الشخصية

opinionParagraph.definition: An opinion paragraph is a short piece of writing where you give your opinion about a topic and support it with reasons and concrete examples.

steps.purpose: State your opinion clearly at the outset.
Explain logically why you hold this particular opinion.
Support your reason with a verifiable example or evidence.
Restate your opinion using refreshed phrasing.

diaryEntry.definition: A diary entry is a personal piece of writing in which you record what happened to you, how you felt, and what you learned from the experience.

components.rule: Write the date and a warm greeting, stating where you were and what you were doing.
components.model: Friday, 21st August - Dear Diary, Today was one of the most challenging days of my life...

components.rule: Describe key events in chronological order using past tenses and time linkers (At first, Then, After that, A few minutes later).
components.model: At first, I was enjoying the scenic trail, but after two hours, fatigue set in.

components.rule: Highlight the moment when conditions became challenging or unexpected problems arose.
components.model: While navigating the steep rocky hill, sudden torrential rain began, challenging our stamina.

components.rule: Detail how the experience concluded, incorporating vivid similes or sensory adjectives.
components.model: When we finally reached safety, my legs felt as heavy as stone, but our hearts were soaring.

components.rule: Reflect on what the ordeal taught you about resilience, friendship, and character.
components.model: This arduous experience taught me that determination can conquer any steep obstacle.

components.rule: Conclude with a succinct, memorable line capturing the enduring essence of the day.
components.model: It was an exhausting expedition, but one unforgettable memory etched in my mind.

grammarStructures.titleEn: Verbs followed by the to-infinitive (to + base form)
grammarStructures.explanation: Certain verbs require an infinitive complement with 'to'. In passive constructions, they take 'to be + past participle'.
examples: Nour decided to join the school orchestra to develop her musical skills.
The workers refused to accept the dangerous safety shortcuts.
She expects to be promoted to team captain next month.

grammarStructures.titleAr: الأفعال المتبوعة بصيغة الـ Gerund (اسم الفاعل V-ing)
grammarStructures.explanation: These verbs are followed directly by a verb ending in -ing. The negative form is formed by placing 'not' directly before the gerund ('not + V-ing').
examples: Many students enjoy creating music or painting in their free time.
She avoids eating processed snacks before intensive athletic training.
He admitted taking the document by mistake and apologized sincerely.
I regret not traveling abroad when the scholarship was accessible.

grammarStructures.titleEn: Verbs with Dual Patterns and Major Meaning Changes
grammarStructures.titleAr: الأفعال التي يتغير معناها تغيراً جوهرياً حسب المصدر أو الـ Gerund
grammarStructures.explanation: Six critical verbs change meaning drastically depending on whether they take 'to + inf' (prospective action / obligation) or 'V-ing' (retrospective memory / past experience).

pairs.toInf: remember to + inf: يتذكر القيام بواجب أو عمل لم يفعله بعد (Remember to lock the front door).
pairs.gerund: remember + V-ing: يتذكر حدثاً أو تجربة وقعت في الماضي (I remember locking the door before leaving).

pairs.toInf: forget to + inf: ينسى أن يؤدي واجباً مطلوباً (She forgot to bring her identification card).
pairs.gerund: forget + V-ing: ينسى أنه فعل شيئاً في الماضي (I'll never forget visiting the Pyramids at sunrise).

pairs.toInf: stop to + inf: يتوقف عن مساره لكي يفعل شيئاً آخر (After walking for hours, they stopped to drink water).
pairs.gerund: stop + V-ing: يمتنع تماماً عن ممارسة عادة أو فعل (He stopped smoking completely last year).

pairs.toInf: regret to + inf: يشعر بالأسف المسبق لإبلاغ خبر مؤسف رسمي (We regret to inform you that your application was rejected).
pairs.gerund: regret + V-ing: يشعر بالندم الشديد على فعل ارتكبه في الماضي (I regret eating so much junk food; now my stomach aches).

pairs.toInf: try to + inf: يبذل جهداً شاقاً للتغلب على صعوبة (She tried to open the rusted jar with all her strength).
pairs.gerund: try + V-ing: يجرب وسيلة أو فكرة ليرى تأثيرها ونتيجتها (If your computer screen freezes, try restarting it).

pairs.toInf: go on to + inf: ينتقل بعد الانتهاء من عمل إلى عمل وموضوع جديد (After discussing screen time, the doctor went on to talk about diet).
pairs.gerund: go on + V-ing: يواصل الاستمرار في نفس العمل دون توقف (The athletes went on running despite heavy rainfall).

grammarStructures.titleEn: Expressions with preposition 'to' followed by V-ing & Bare Infinitive Rules
grammarStructures.titleAr: تراكيب تنتهي بحرف الجر to ويليها V-ing، وقواعد المصدر المجرد بدون to
grammarStructures.explanation: In standard English, the preposition 'to' is followed by a noun or gerund in fixed idioms. Conversely, verbs of perception and modal-like causatives take the bare infinitive.
toPrepositionList: look forward to + V-ing (يتطلع بشوق إلى)
be/get used to + V-ing (معتاد على في الحاضر)
owing to / due to + V-ing (بسبب / ناتج عن)
be opposed to + V-ing (يعارض / مناهض لـ)
bareInfinitiveRules: had better + bare inf ('You had better rest now')
would rather + bare inf ('I would rather stay indoors')
let + object + bare inf ('She let him borrow the camera')
make + object + bare inf in active ('The teacher made Ali repeat the task')
be made + to-inf in passive ('Ali was made to repeat the task')

exercises.questionText: Nour decided ________ the school orchestra to develop her musical skills.
exercises.explanation: The verb 'decide' is followed by the to-infinitive ('decide to do something').

exercises.questionText: Many students enjoy ________ music or painting in their free time.
exercises.explanation: 'Enjoy' is always followed by a gerund ('enjoy doing something').

exercises.questionText: I promised ________ my homework carefully before dinner.
exercises.explanation: 'Promise' is followed by 'to + inf'.

exercises.questionText: She avoids ________ processed food before intensive athletic training.
exercises.explanation: 'Avoid' is followed by a gerund ('avoid doing something').

exercises.questionText: The students agreed ________ part in the local environmental campaign.
exercises.explanation: 'Agree' takes 'to + base verb'.

exercises.questionText: The teacher encouraged students ________ creative solutions to community problems.
exercises.explanation: 'Encourage + object + to-infinitive' is the correct verb pattern.

exercises.questionText: They finished ________ the theatrical play an hour ago.
exercises.explanation: 'Finish' is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

exercises.questionText: The factory workers refused ________ the hazardous new safety shortcuts.
exercises.explanation: 'Refuse' is followed by 'to + infinitive'.

exercises.questionText: Astronomers hope ________ new habitable exoplanets soon.
exercises.explanation: 'Hope' takes 'to + infinitive'.

exercises.questionText: Do you mind ________ this difficult philosophical concept once again?
exercises.explanation: 'Mind' or 'Would you mind' is followed by V-ing.

exercises.questionText: She is busy ________ her research project, so please do not interrupt her.
exercises.explanation: 'Be busy' is an idiomatic phrase followed directly by V-ing.

exercises.questionText: My father allowed me ________ his laptop twice a week for online research.
exercises.explanation: 'Allow + object + to + inf'.

exercises.questionText: The suspect denied ________ the window of the antique store.
exercises.explanation: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund ('deny doing something').

exercises.questionText: The student admitted ________ his homework notebook at home by mistake.
exercises.explanation: 'Admit' is followed by V-ing.

exercises.questionText: The researcher tends ________ late hours when analyzing atomic structures.
exercises.explanation: 'Tend' is followed by 'to + inf'.

exercises.questionText: Her scientific team plans ________ a new Earth-monitoring satellite next year.
exercises.explanation: 'Plan' takes 'to + base verb'.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly shows the meaning: 'he stopped a habit completely'?
exercises.explanation: 'Stop + V-ing' means giving up a habit or activity permanently, whereas 'stop to + inf' means pausing an activity in order to do another.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence means: 'he paused his journey in order to have a coffee'?
options: After working for three hours, he stopped having coffee.
After working for three hours, he stopped to have a cup of coffee.
After working for three hours, he stopped have a cup of coffee.
After working for three hours, he stopped had a cup of coffee.
exercises.correctAnswer: After working for three hours, he stopped to have a cup of coffee.
exercises.explanation: 'Stop to have' indicates the purpose of pausing.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'remember' for a past action already done?
options: I remember to lock the door.
exercises.explanation: 'Remember + V-ing' refers to looking back at a memory of an action completed in the past.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'remember' for a future obligation?
exercises.explanation: 'Remember to + inf' is used for reminders and prospective duties.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'try' to mean 'make an experiment to see what happens'?
options: If the software freezes, try to restart your PC.
If the software freezes, try restarting your PC.
If the software freezes, try restart your PC.
If the software freezes, try restarted your PC.
exercises.correctAnswer: If the software freezes, try restarting your PC.
exercises.explanation: 'Try + V-ing' means trying a method or experiment to see if it solves a problem.

exercises.questionText: 'He stopped smoking last year after his illness.' This means that:
options: he paused what he was doing in order to smoke.
he no longer smokes at all now.
he forgot that he used to smoke.
exercises.correctAnswer: he no longer smokes at all now.
exercises.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' expresses total cessation of a habitual behavior.

exercises.questionText: 'I remember locking the door before we left the house.' This means that:
options: I have a clear memory of the action of locking the door in the past.
I am reminding myself to lock the door in the future.
I forgot whether I locked the door or not.
someone else reminded me to lock the door.
exercises.correctAnswer: I have a clear memory of the action of locking the door in the past.
exercises.explanation: 'Remember + V-ing' is retrospective recall.

exercises.questionText: Which sentence correctly rewrites: 'It was a mistake to eat so much cake, and now I feel sick'?
options: I regret to eat so much cake.
I regret eating so much cake.
I regret to have eaten so much cake.
I regret ate so much cake.
exercises.correctAnswer: I regret eating so much cake.
exercises.explanation: 'Regret + V-ing' expresses penitence and sorrow over a past action.

exercises.questionText: The athlete was accustomed to ________ for six hours every day.
exercises.explanation: 'Be accustomed to' contains the preposition 'to', which must be followed by a gerund ('training').

exercises.questionText: Positive feedback from teachers can improve students' self-esteem. What does self-esteem mean?
options: The ability to control other people.
The way people feel about their own value and abilities.
The desire to become more popular online.
The tendency to compare different cultures.
exercises.correctAnswer: The way people feel about their own value and abilities.
exercises.explanation: Self-esteem refers to self-worth and confidence in one's personal identity and capabilities.

exercises.questionText: After suffering a muscle tear, the athlete decided to withdraw from the competition. What is the clearest example of 'withdraw'?
options: A student leaves a debate team before the final round.
A player trains harder before an important match.
A runner joins an additional race at the weekend.
A musician continues performing despite feeling nervous.
exercises.correctAnswer: A student leaves a debate team before the final round.
exercises.explanation: 'Withdraw' means to pull out, remove oneself, or disengage from participation.

exercises.questionText: The actors attended a final rehearsal before performing for a large audience. What does rehearsal mean?
options: The official performance before an audience.
A celebration held after a successful performance.
A practice session held before the real performance.
A written review of an artistic event.
exercises.correctAnswer: A practice session held before the real performance.
exercises.explanation: 'Rehearsal' is a trial performance or practice session before a public staging.

exercises.questionText: Mountain climbers need great endurance in extreme weather. Which situation is the clearest example of 'endurance'?
options: A swimmer continues a long-distance race despite becoming tired.
A runner stops after a few minutes because the race feels difficult.
A cyclist chooses only very short and easy routes.
An athlete avoids training whenever the weather is unpleasant.
exercises.correctAnswer: A swimmer continues a long-distance race despite becoming tired.
exercises.explanation: 'Endurance' is the ability to persist through prolonged physical hardship and fatigue.

exercises.questionText: Strong motivation helps students persevere toward difficult goals. The underlined noun has an antonymous meaning to:
exercises.explanation: 'Motivation' means drive/incentive; its exact antonym is 'discouragement'.

correctTheFormExercises.sentence: Many parents worry that their children have become ________ (addict) to video games.
Spending time outdoors instead of on screens can bring real ________ (fulfilling) to a teenager's life.
Experts recommend finding a ________ (balance) routine between online and offline activities.
The effect of gaming on mental health remains a highly ________ (debate) topic among researchers.
Some countries are considering stricter ________ (regulate) of screen time for young users.
Streaming apps are designed to be extremely ________ (entertain), making them difficult to stop using.
Team-based video games can improve a player's hand-eye ________ (coordinate).
Ignoring screen-time limits can be quite ________ (risk) for a teenager's sleep and concentration.
Digital tools can also boost ________ (create) thinking when used in moderation.

jreTrueFalseExercises.passage: Platforms like Instagram and TikTok present carefully chosen images of people's lives, making it easy for young users to compare themselves negatively to others. Studies suggest that heavy social media use is linked to increased feelings of anxiety, loneliness, and depression, particularly among teenagers.
jreTrueFalseExercises.statement: Social media use has no effect on teenagers' mood.
jreTrueFalseExercises.justification: False. The text explicitly states that heavy social media use is directly linked to increased feelings of anxiety, loneliness, and depression.

jreTrueFalseExercises.passage: Access to sports facilities and resources varies greatly by cost and location, which creates structural barriers preventing many students from regular athletic participation.
jreTrueFalseExercises.statement: According to the text, all young people have equal access to sports facilities and resources.
jreTrueFalseExercises.justification: False. Access is unequal and depends on cost and geographic location, leaving many youth with structural barriers.

jreTrueFalseExercises.passage: Research consistently shows that taking regular breaks from screens can improve mood, concentration, and sleep quality. Outdoor activities, face-to-face socializing, and creative hobbies all provide benefits that screens simply cannot replicate.
jreTrueFalseExercises.statement: Taking regular breaks from screens has a beneficial effect on concentration.
jreTrueFalseExercises.justification: True. The study proves that regular screen breaks improve mood, concentration, and sleep quality.

jreTrueFalseExercises.passage: The World Health Organization officially recognized gaming disorder as an addictive mental health condition in 2019, highlighting the risks of uncontrolled gaming.
jreTrueFalseExercises.statement: Gaming disorder has never been officially recognized as a mental health condition.
jreTrueFalseExercises.justification: False. The WHO officially classified it as a clinical mental health condition in 2019.
